note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, lighting answer, hours rule and address below comes from the City of Rockville's own pages: the table under "Outdoor Pickleball Courts" on its Pickleball Courts and Programs page for the counts and the Lighted column, and each park's own place page for the address, the parking and the amenities. The table's count cell is quoted in the City's words, which separate "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" from "pickleball lines on" tennis courts, and every row is re-asserted on every build. Where the City stays silent - on price, on surface, on nets at three venues - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: Rockville answers the parking question park by park, and for once the answers include a no. Calvin Park's page states it outright: "Calvin Park does not have parking. Access to park amenities is available via pathways connecting to city sidewalks and roads." The two courts there are reached on foot, or by the bike path the City says runs along Baltimore Road. At the other end, five parks are described as having "plenty of parking": Broome Athletic Park, Dogwood Park, Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park, Potomac Woods Park, where the City puts the lot at 2276 Dunster Lane off Stratton Drive, and Welsh Park. Hillcrest Park is more specific still - parking spaces at the east entrance on Crawford Drive, street parking at the west. Every park page with an accessible-features table counts its accessible spaces: eight at Fallsgrove, Stepanek and Rockville Civic Center Park, six at Broome and Dogwood, four at Isreal, three at Potomac Woods, two at Welsh, one at Hillcrest. North Farm Park and Rockcrest Park say nothing about parking either way, and this site records nothing for them. Restrooms follow a pattern worth knowing before a long session. At Calvin, Dogwood, Hillcrest, North Farm and Potomac Woods the City notes that "restrooms are available only with a permit", which means a pavilion booking, not a drop-in game. Isreal Park's new pavilion has two accessible restrooms in the City's own list. Broome, Dogwood and Stepanek mention drinking fountains.
slots.peak_hours: The City sets one clock for every outdoor court in its table and then qualifies it twice. The rule is "Courts are open from dawn to dusk and are available on a first-come, first-served basis." The first qualification is lighting: "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m.", and the Lighted column reads Yes at four published venues - Broome Athletic Park, Dogwood Park, Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park and Welsh Park, nineteen courts between them. That is the after-work window in Rockville, and it is a published one rather than a guess; the other eight venues are marked No, so twenty-seven courts end at dusk by the City's own answer. The second qualification is the one a first-come player can trip over: "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts, so some may be reserved for class use and closed to the public." The City runs adult, youth, family and private pickleball lessons and a league, and each row of its table carries a "View Schedule" link under a Court Schedule column. Those schedules have not been read for this page, so which courts are closed for class, and when, is not published here. One session time is on the page itself: "Social play is held at Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park from 10 a.m.-12 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays", with players rotated so everyone gets on court. If you want the four dedicated courts at Stepanek to yourselves, those are the mornings to avoid; if you want a game without bringing three friends, they are the mornings to go. The park pages give a second phrasing, "Open Sunrise to Sunset", for the park rather than the court. Nothing more about busy times is stated, and it is not supplied here from habit.
slots.surface_condition: The word surface does not appear on the City's pickleball page or on any of the twelve park pages, so nothing about what these courts are made of is published here. What the City does say about the courts is more useful than a material, because it says what kind of court each one is. Twelve of the forty-six are "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" in the table's own words - four at Broome Athletic Park, four at Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park, two at Isreal Park and two at Welsh Park - built for the game, with no tennis lines to read past. Thirty-one are "pickleball lines on" tennis courts at nine venues, two games to a tennis court everywhere except Dogwood's single court, which is one game played over the tennis net. Rockcrest Park's three carry neither phrase and are counted without being split. The net is the other stated fact. Nine venues say "bring your own net"; Dogwood's row says "use tennis net" on one court and bring your own on the other four, so that venue publishes no net answer; Broome and Stepanek, the two dedicated-only rows, say nothing about nets at all. Two park pages mention a rally wall beside the lined tennis courts, at Potomac Woods Park and Rockville Civic Center Park. The park pages date playgrounds - Isreal's installed in 2024, Potomac Woods' in 2023, Rockcrest's new for 2024 - and date no court, so how new any slab is stays unstated.
slots.local_scene: Forty-six verified courts at twelve City parks, every one of them outdoor under the heading the City gives its table, "Outdoor Pickleball Courts", and every one with a lighting answer, because the table has a Lighted column and completes it with Yes or No on every row. That column is the reason Rockville reads so cleanly here: four venues lit, eight stated unlit, none unknown. What the City does not write anywhere is a price. Neither the pickleball page nor any park page prints a fee, and none prints the word free, so no Rockville venue is recorded as free and there is no free page for the city. Two rows of the City's own table are not published. Twinbrook Park has "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)" and Lighted Yes, and the City puts it at "12920 Twinbrook Parkway", a house number that neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap has any record of; a count-bearing address that does not resolve as the operator writes it is not published. Glenora Park has four courts on two tennis courts and its Address block reads "Dundee Road and Wootton Parkway", an intersection with no house number, which the address check cannot take. Both are re-read every build and publish the day the City prints an address that resolves. The page also names Lincoln Park Community Center, Thomas Farm Community Center and Twinbrook Community Recreation Center for "open gym schedules during drop-in hours featuring pickleball", with no court count, so they are named here and not listed. Around the courts there is a programme: adult, youth and family classes, private lessons, five named instructors, league play, and a social session four mornings a week at Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park. Rockville is the first city in Maryland and the first in Montgomery County on this site.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under lights
best_for.text: Welsh Park holds six courts, the largest set in Rockville: "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted Yes, so play runs to 10 p.m. The park page adds a 33.3-acre sports park next to the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center, with plenty of parking. Bring a net for the four lined courts.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a real pickleball court and a guaranteed game
best_for.text: Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park has "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", lit, closing at 10 p.m., in a 26.29-acre park at the north end of King Farm with plenty of parking. It is also where the City holds social play, 10 a.m. to noon on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, rotating players so everyone gets a game. The City says nothing about nets here, and nothing about price.

best_for.heading: Best if you play in daylight and want restrooms you can use
best_for.text: Isreal Park - the City's spelling - has "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" and two more lined on a tennis court, four in all, Lighted No, so it closes at dusk. It adjoins the Lincoln Park Community Center, one of three centres the City names for drop-in gym pickleball, and its pavilion has two accessible restrooms and four accessible parking spaces. Bring a net for the lined pair.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Rockville have?
faqs.a: We have verified 46 across twelve City parks: six at Welsh, five at Dogwood, four each at Broome, Fallsgrove, Isreal, Mattie J.T. Stepanek, North Farm, Potomac Woods and Rockville Civic Center Park, three at Rockcrest, and two each at Calvin and Hillcrest. The City's table lists two more parks, Twinbrook and Glenora, with four courts each, which we cannot publish because their addresses do not resolve.

Broome Athletic Park, Dogwood Park, Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park and Welsh Park - nineteen courts - and the City adds that "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m." The other eight venues are marked No in the table's Lighted column, which is a stated answer rather than a gap, so their courts end at dusk. Twinbrook Park is marked Yes too, but its address resolves nowhere.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Rockville?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City prints no price on its pickleball page or on any park page, and it does not write the word free, so no Rockville venue is recorded as free and there is no free page for the city. What the City does write is the access rule: first come, first served, with City programmes taking priority and some courts closed for class use.

faqs.q: Why are Twinbrook Park and Glenora Park not listed?
faqs.a: Both are rows in the City's table. Twinbrook Park, four lit courts on two tennis courts, is at "12920 Twinbrook Parkway", a house number neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find. Glenora Park, four unlit courts, has "Dundee Road and Wootton Parkway" in its Address block, an intersection with no house number. A venue at an address that does not resolve is not published, and both are re-read every build.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: At nine venues, yes, and the City says so in the table: "bring your own net". Dogwood's row says "use tennis net" on one court and bring your own on the other four, so no net answer is published there. Broome and Stepanek, whose rows say only "Dedicated Pickleball Courts", say nothing about nets. Twelve of the 46 courts are dedicated; 31 are lines on tennis courts, two games per tennis court.
